open_threads: RULED 2026-07-31, recorded so nobody re-opens it: THE STALENESS THRESHOLD IS 5 SECONDS — five missed ticks at a once-per-second cadence, and the cadence is ratified by the same breath ('a tick that's once a second'; the original 'lets say' hedge is spent). LIVE = last-run within 5s; DEAD = older, whatever the record claims about its state or its pid. Presence is not liveness. Written into all four ground-loop tickets and into the decision file's what_is_settled. Three times the interval is the standard liveness heuristic; five gives slack for a loaded box.

WATCHME(liveness-read) WAS CARRIED AND THEN DROPPED, replaced by 'none, because...'. I had cast a watch to calibrate the threshold 'from evidence rather than a guess.' Akien: 'oh my fucking god. what do you INFER would be a good threshold for a tick that's once a second?' Earned. A probe carried to learn a settled constant is a standing pulse cost against a settled answer — Law 1's defect wearing a probe's clothes. Recorded here because the SHAPE recurs: before escalating a gap into a watch/ticket/question, try answering it. If a competent engineer would state a default from standard practice, state the number.

STILL OPEN AND REAL — THE ATOMIC CLAIM. Two entry points can both read DEAD inside the same 5s window and both start a loop, because read-then-act is not atomic. The claim must be (O_EXCL create or equivalent). Asymmetric and that is why it matters: a missed start is visible, a double start fires every callback twice. Ticket an-entry-point-starts-the-loop-only-once. This is the last unsettled thing in that corner.
